title: The Four-Winged Dinosaur That Hunted Early Birds
hook: Piles of crushed bird bones from ancient China had no obvious culprit. Meet Jian changmaensis: a four-winged, gliding cousin of Velociraptor that may have hunted Earth's earliest birds.
key_points: A newly described feathered dinosaur, Jian changmaensis, has been identified in China.
It was a four-winged glider, with flight feathers on both its arms and legs.
It's a close cousin of Velociraptor and lived alongside early birds.
It may be the predator behind mysterious piles of crushed prehistoric bird bones.
The find shows how closely early birds and bird-like dinosaurs overlapped.
content_html: Paleontologists had a whodunit on their hands: piles of crushed prehistoric bird bones in China, with no clear predator to blame. A new study reported via ScienceDaily names a suspect — a newly discovered feathered dinosaur called Jian changmaensis.
extra_html: Jian was a four-winged glider, sporting flight feathers not just on its arms but on its legs too — a body plan that sits squarely on the blurry boundary between dinosaur and bird. A close cousin of Velociraptor, it shared its world with the very early birds whose remains pile up in the fossil record, making it a plausible culprit for those crushed bones. More than a single predator story, the find fleshes out a landscape where bird-like dinosaurs and true early birds lived side by side, experimenting with feathers and flight at the same time. It's another data point in one of evolution's best-documented transitions — the long, feathered road from dinosaurs to the birds at your feeder.

related.title: The Evidence for Evolution
related.hook: Fossils, DNA, shared body plans, and change we can watch happen — evolution isn't a hunch, it's a conclusion forced by many independent lines of evidence.

related.title: The History of Life
related.hook: Life is about 3.5 billion years old, but for most of that time it was just microbes. Animals, plants, and us are latecomers crowded into the most recent slice of deep time.

flashcards.prompt: What was unusual about Jian changmaensis's body?

choices.text: It had four wings — feathers on both its arms and legs — and could glide
It had no feathers at all

flashcards.explanation_html: Jian was a four-winged glider, with flight feathers on both fore- and hind-limbs — a body plan that blurs the dinosaur–bird line.

flashcards.prompt: Why is this dinosaur scientifically interesting?
flashcards.back_html: As a feathered, gliding cousin of Velociraptor living among early birds, it shows how closely dinosaurs and birds overlapped in the same ancient landscape.

flashcards.prompt: What mystery might Jian help explain?

choices.text: Piles of crushed early-bird bones — it may have been the predator
Why all the dinosaurs went extinct
The origin of the first mammals

flashcards.explanation_html: Researchers suggest Jian could be the missing predator responsible for the crushed prehistoric bird bones found in China.
